body:
The situation is even worse when reproducing this on Linux using OS file manager (such as Nemo/Nautilus). I even discovered a similar preview bug in Nemo.

When importing a project using godot, the timestamps of all files in the project are almost same (`find -name *.png | xargs stat`). 

<details>

<summary>stat outputs (all png files)</summary>

```bash
  File: ./assets/other_rocks/rock1.png
  Size: 3256      	Blocks: 8          IO Block: 4096   regular file
Device: 0,44	Inode: 2658710     Links: 1
Access: (0664/-rw-rw-r--)  Uid: ( 1000/     bee)   Gid: ( 1000/     bee)
Access: 2026-03-16 13:06:45.460001595 +0800
Modify: 2026-03-16 13:06:43.205035720 +0800
Change: 2026-03-16 13:06:43.205035720 +0800
 Birth: 2026-03-16 13:06:43.204832250 +0800
  File: ./assets/other_rocks/rock2.png
  Size: 4614      	Blocks: 16         IO Block: 4096   regular file
Device: 0,44	Inode: 2658712     Links: 1
Access: (0664/-rw-rw-r--)  Uid: ( 1000/     bee)   Gid: ( 1000/     bee)
Access: 2026-03-16 13:06:45.460001595 +0800
Modify: 2026-03-16 13:06:43.205220703 +0800
Change: 2026-03-16 13:06:43.205220703 +0800
 Birth: 2026-03-16 13:06:43.205180855 +0800
  File: ./assets/tiles/rock.png
  Size: 4614      	Blocks: 16         IO Block: 4096   regular file
Device: 0,44	Inode: 2658715     Links: 1
Access: (0664/-rw-rw-r--)  Uid: ( 1000/     bee)   Gid: ( 1000/     bee)
Access: 2026-03-16 13:06:45.460001595 +0800
Modify: 2026-03-16 13:06:43.205348966 +0800
Change: 2026-03-16 13:06:43.205348966 +0800
 Birth: 2026-03-16 13:06:43.205270852 +0800
```
</details>

In Nemo, when using `rock1.png` to overwrite `rock.png`:
1. Copy/move `rock1.png` to the `tiles` directory;
2. Remove `rock.png`;
3. Rename `rock1.png` to `rock.png`.

<details>

<summary>stat outputs (rock.png, overwrite in Nemo)</summary>

```bash
  File: ./assets/tiles/rock.png
  Size: 3256      	Blocks: 8          IO Block: 4096   regular file
Device: 0,44	Inode: 2658987     Links: 1
Access: (0664/-rw-rw-r--)  Uid: ( 1000/     bee)   Gid: ( 1000/     bee)
Access: 2026-03-16 13:07:39.883896376 +0800
Modify: 2026-03-16 13:06:43.205035720 +0800  # The mtime timestamp remains same as rock1.png.
Change: 2026-03-16 13:07:42.694145501 +0800
 Birth: 2026-03-16 13:07:39.662876765 +0800
```
</details>

This appears to differ little from overwriting using `cp -p` or `mv`, as almost all of them leave the `mtime` unchanged.

<details>

<summary>stat outputs (rock.png, overwrite using cp -p)</summary>

```bash
cp -p assets/other_rocks/rock1.png assets/tiles/rock.png
```

```
  File: ./assets/tiles/rock.png
  Size: 3256      	Blocks: 8          IO Block: 4096   regular file
Device: 0,44	Inode: 2658987     Links: 1
Access: (0664/-rw-rw-r--)  Uid: ( 1000/     bee)   Gid: ( 1000/     bee)
Access: 2026-03-16 13:06:45.460001595 +0800
Modify: 2026-03-16 13:06:43.205035720 +0800
Change: 2026-03-16 13:08:26.378479969 +0800
 Birth: 2026-03-16 13:07:39.662876765 +0800
```
</details>


<details>

<summary>stat outputs (rock.png, overwrite using mv)</summary>

```bash
mv  assets/other_rocks/rock1.png assets/tiles/rock.png
```

```
  File: ./assets/tiles/rock.png
  Size: 3256      	Blocks: 8          IO Block: 4096   regular file
Device: 0,44	Inode: 2658710     Links: 1
Access: (0664/-rw-rw-r--)  Uid: ( 1000/     bee)   Gid: ( 1000/     bee)
Access: 2026-03-16 13:06:45.460001595 +0800
Modify: 2026-03-16 13:06:43.205035720 +0800
Change: 2026-03-16 13:08:49.667985737 +0800
 Birth: 2026-03-16 13:06:43.204832250 +0800
```
</details>

This results in the editor not recognizing that `rock.png` has been updated, even after restarting the editor.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/db5da10d21bad1691865b188c55a208d26ad3b33/drivers/unix/file_access_unix.cpp#L373-L387

The timestamps for directories are the same as well.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/db5da10d21bad1691865b188c55a208d26ad3b33/drivers/unix/dir_access_unix.cpp#L140

If there is no plan to implement a method for retrieving `ctime`, perhaps `get_modified_time()` should return the **maximum** of `mtime` and `ctime`.
